title: Award-Winning Texas Cook-Off Chili
time: About 2 to 2.5 hours
summary: Pete's chili that took first place at a Texas state cook-off in 2006. He has posted this same pot more than once; viewers have also used it to win their own cook-offs.

ingredients.text: 1 lb hot breakfast sausage (Jimmy Dean Hot)
3 fresh jalapeños, chopped (some videos of this same recipe use 2 large jalapeños)
2 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (his own blend)
3 cans (15.5 oz each) Bush's Chili Magic, Campfire Style
Splash of Pepperbellypete's Zippy Zap (optional, to finish)

instructions: In a 12-quart pot, brown the ground beef and drain it.
Add the hot breakfast sausage (don't drain) and the tomato paste. Break everything up and cook until the sausage is fully done and the paste has cooked in.
Add the onion, jalapeños, garlic, Hatch green chiles, Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, and Williams chili seasoning. Stir and cook about 5 minutes, until the vegetables start to soften.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and tomato sauce. Cover and simmer on low for at least 1 hour (Pete went 1.5 hours).
Stir in the Bush's Chili Magic, cover again, and simmer another 30 minutes.
Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap and serve.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
The written version is on page 177 of Pete's cookbook.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/mUkmgYiTkPY and https://www.youtube.com/shorts/m68vDW-z0Bg

title: Cook-Off Chili with Pete's Tweaks
time: About 1.5 hours, plus browning
summary: The same cook-off chili with a few changes Pete says might help you take first and second place: fire-roasted Rotel, beef broth, Worcestershire, and a little yellow mustard.

ingredients.text: 1 lb hot breakfast sausage (Jimmy Dean Hot)
2 fresh jalapeños, chopped, seeds and all
3 packets (1 oz each) Williams Original Chili Seasoning
3 cans (15.5 oz each) Bush's Chili Magic, Campfire Style
Splash of Pepperbellypete's Zippy Zap (optional, to finish)

instructions: In a 10-quart pot, start browning the ground beef. While it cooks, add the Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste.
Add the hot breakfast sausage, onion, jalapeños, and Williams chili seasoning. Cook until the meat is fully done.
Stir in the fire-roasted Rotel, petite diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, beef broth, and minced garlic.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 1 hour.
Stir in the Bush's Chili Magic and yellow mustard. Cover and simmer on low at least 30 minutes more.
Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Pete presents this as a couple of small changes to his winning cook-off chili.
Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Crockpot Cook-Off Chili
time: 3 hours on high or 6 hours on low, plus browning
summary: The award-winning cook-off chili adapted for the crockpot. Brown the meats first, then load everything into a 10-quart slow cooker.

ingredients.text: 3 cans (15.5 oz each) Bush's Chili Magic, Campfire Style
Splash of Pepperbellypete's Zippy Zap (optional, to finish)

instructions: In a skillet, brown and drain the ground beef.
Add the breakfast sausage and tomato paste. Cook until the sausage is fully done; do not drain.
Transfer the meat to a 10-quart crockpot.
Add the onion, jalapeños, Hatch green chiles, garlic, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, Williams chili seasoning, and Bush's Chili Magic. Stir well.
Cover and cook on high for 3 hours or on low for 6 hours.
Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap before serving.
notes: This is the cook-off chili packed into a crockpot, with the Chili Magic added at the start instead of at the end.
Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Homestyle Cook-Off Chili
time: About 2.5 hours
summary: Another cook-off version of Pete's chili, this time with Rotel and beef broth in place of the big cans of tomato sauce, and a longer simmer.

ingredients.text: 3 packets (1 oz each) Williams Original Chili Seasoning
About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (his own blend)
3 cans (15.5 oz each) Bush's Chili Magic

instructions: Brown and drain the ground beef.
Add the breakfast sausage and tomato paste, and cook together.
Add the onion, jalapeños, garlic, Hatch green chiles, Williams chili seasoning, and Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, Rotel, and beef broth. Bring to a simmer on medium-low and cook 2 hours.
Stir in the Bush's Chili Magic, cover, and cook at least 30 minutes more.
notes: Pete says the written recipe is on page 177 of his cookbook. The liquids here differ from the 44-oz tomato sauce version of that same cook-off chili.
Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning is Pete's own blend; use your favorite seasoning blend if you don't have it.

title: Chili-Grind Chili with Beer
time: About 3 hours, plus browning
summary: A bigger, beer-and-broth pot made with chili-grind beef instead of the usual ground beef and sausage mix.

ingredients.text: 6 oz chili paste (the audio may be 'tomato paste'; 6 oz is the amount)
31 oz Bush's Chili Magic (about two 15.5 oz cans)

instructions: Brown the chili-grind beef.
Add the chili paste (or tomato paste), onion, jalapeños, Williams chili seasoning, and garlic.
Pour in the beer and scrape up the browned bits on the bottom of the pot.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, Hatch green chiles, tomato sauce, stone-ground mustard, and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 2 hours.
Stir in the Chili Magic and Zippy Zap. Cover and simmer 1 hour more.
notes: The transcript sounds like 'chili paste' right after the meat browns; in Pete's other chilis this step is 6 oz tomato paste, so use that if chili paste is unclear.
Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Competition-Style Hot Dog Chili
time: About 2.5 to 3 hours
summary: A smooth, competition-style chili with everything but the sirloin pureed, thickened with oatmeal and refried beans, and meant to be ladled over a hot dog.

ingredients.text: 3 packets (1 oz each) Williams Original Chili Seasoning
15 oz refried beans (Pete prefers the packet over the can)

instructions: In an 8-quart pot, add a splash of olive oil and the ground sirloin.
Add the Worcestershire, pureed Hatch green chiles, onion, jalapeños, and Rotel, plus the garlic, tomato paste, Williams chili seasoning, beef stock, and oatmeal.
Stir well and break the meat up. Cover and cook on low for 1 hour.
Stir in the refried beans, yellow mustard, and Zippy Zap.
Cover and cook on low 1.5 hours more, stirring about every 30 minutes.
After 2.5 to 3 hours total, it should be thick enough to spoon over a hot dog.
notes: Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.
The oatmeal is a competition-chili thickener; use a 1 oz packet as stated, not a breakfast bowl of oats.

title: Hamburger Chili Dog Chili
time: About 2.5 hours, plus browning
summary: A five-pound pot of hamburger chili with ketchup, mustard, and broth, simmered until it's ready for a chili dog. Pete also posted this same recipe as hamburger chili.

ingredients.text: 1 large yellow onion (part of the 'Texas Trinity')

instructions: Brown the ground beef, breaking it up well, then drain it. Pete wraps foil around the strainer so the grease doesn't go down the drain.

Add the onion, jalapeños, garlic, Worcestershire, chili powder, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, cumin, bay leaf, Zippy Zap, and tomato paste. Mix well and cook about 10 minutes on medium heat.
Stir in the fire-roasted tomatoes, Rotel, beef broth, mustard, and ketchup.
Bring to a low simmer, cover, and cook 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
notes: Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/SXO77xGvt3M

title: Pete's Favorite Chili
time: About 1 hour simmering, plus browning
summary: The chili Pete calls his favorite: beef and pan sausage with Rotel, ranch-style beans, and a can of Chili Magic.

ingredients.text: 2 packets (1 oz each) chili seasoning (your favorite)

instructions: Cook the ground beef and sausage until the meat is done all the way through, then strain the meat and set it aside.
In the pot, cook the onion and jalapeños with the Worcestershire and tomato paste.
Return the meat to the pot. Add the Rotel, garlic, chili seasoning, tomato sauce, Bush's Chili Magic, ranch-style beans, Zippy Zap, and beef broth.
Leave it on and simmer 1 hour.
notes: Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.
He doesn't name a brand of chili seasoning in this video, just two 1-oz packets of your favorite.

title: White Chicken Chili
time: About 1.5 hours on high or 3 hours on low
summary: A crockpot white chicken chili with a rotisserie garlic-herb chicken, white kidney beans, roasted Hatch chiles, and cream cheese.

ingredients.text: 1 fully cooked, deboned garlic-herb rotisserie chicken (Pete uses a grocery-store roasted chicken)
3 cans (15.5 oz each) white kidney beans, rinsed
4 ears fresh corn, kernels cut off (or 1 can of corn)
Splash of hot sauce, to taste (Pete adds 'Heat Blast')

instructions: Add the onion, fire-roasted tomatoes, Hatch green chiles, rinsed beans, oregano, coriander, cumin, black pepper, chili-lime adobo, garlic powder, smoked paprika, cream cheese, corn, cilantro, lime juice, fajita seasoning, chicken broth, and the deboned chicken to the crockpot.
Stir well, cover, and cook on high about 1.5 hours, stirring every 30 minutes, or about 3 hours on low.
Finish with a splash of hot sauce if you want it spicier.
notes: Pete jokes that cilantro is 'soap on a rope' to some people; leave it out if you're one of them.
He finishes his bowl with a splash of something he calls Heat Blast; the exact product isn't clearly identified, so use your favorite hot sauce.

title: Ranch Chicken Chili
time: About 50 minutes
summary: A quick chicken chili with ranch and taco seasoning, black beans, ranch-style beans, corn, and cream cheese, served over tortilla chips.

ingredients.text: Shredded cheese, for topping (amount not specified)

instructions: Add the chicken broth, onion, jalapeños, and garlic to a pot (the Texas Trinity in the broth). Simmer about 20 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, Rotel, corn, black beans, ranch-style beans, taco seasoning, ranch seasoning, cream cheese, chopped rotisserie chicken, and Zippy Zap.
Once everything is incorporated, simmer about 30 minutes.
Serve over tortilla chips, top with shredded cheese, and add habanero sauce if you like.
notes: Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; he mentions it's on Amazon or eBay. Use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: White Chicken Chili Mac & Cheese
time: About 30 minutes in a 350°F oven, plus a 2-minute broil, and stovetop time
summary: A baked white-chicken chili mac with a Hatch chile and Rotel cheese sauce, rotisserie chicken, and a Colby Jack topping.

ingredients.text: 32 oz white American cheese (from the grocery store deli)
Colby Jack cheese, for topping (amount not specified)

instructions: Melt the butter and cook the onion and jalapeño until completely soft.
Add the Hatch green chiles, fire-roasted Rotel, garlic, chili powder, black pepper, garlic powder, and Worcestershire. Stir and cook a few minutes.
Add the white American cheese and evaporated milk. Keep stirring until the cheese is fully melted.
Stir in the chopped rotisserie chicken and the drained macaroni until everything is well combined.
Top with Colby Jack. Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes, then broil 2 minutes.
notes: The audio is a little muddy on Worcestershire ('washi sister sauce') and Colby Jack ('Kobe Jack'); those are the standard names for what he appears to say.
He says you can get the white American cheese from the grocery store deli.

title: Poor Man's Chili Mac
time: About 30 minutes simmering, plus boiling the pasta
summary: An old-school, tight-budget chili mac: a tomato-chili beef sauce simmered with sink water, then tossed with jumbo elbows and a little cheese.

ingredients.text: 3 1/2 cups water (Pete calls it '117-degree clear sink water')

instructions: Brown the ground beef, breaking it up well. Stir in the tomato paste and let it cook with the beef.
Add the onion, garlic powder, chili powder, cumin, ground red pepper, and smoked paprika.
Stir in the water and chili-style tomatoes. Bring to a simmer and cook 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, salt a pot of boiling water and cook the jumbo elbows 6 to 7 minutes. Drain.
Taste the sauce and add salt as you like. Turn the heat off, add the noodles, and stir them in.
Finish with a splash of habanero sauce and a little cheese if you want. Pete also likes it in a fold-over sandwich.
notes: Amounts for the ground red pepper and smoked paprika were not given separately from the 1/2 tbsp cumin.

title: Chili Mac & Cheese
time: Until the pasta is cooked the way you like it
summary: A one-pot chili mac: seasoned ground meat, crushed tomatoes, chili beans, and rotini that cook right in the sauce, finished with cheese.
instructions: Heat a splash of olive oil and brown the ground meat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and jalapeño, then the cumin, cayenne, black pepper, garlic salt, smoked paprika, and chili powder.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, pasta, chili beans, and beef broth.
Cover and simmer until the pasta is cooked the way you like it.
Take it off the heat and stir in the cheese.
notes: Pete uses rotini because, in his words, elbow noodles are ugly. Use whatever pasta you like.

title: Green Chile Stew
time: About 2.5 hours
summary: A Hatch green chile stew with pork shoulder, hot sausage, potatoes, and ranch seasoning, simmered until it's thick enough to scoop with pork rinds.

ingredients.text: About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (his own blend)
32 oz roasted, peeled, and pureed Hatch green chiles

instructions: Cook the pork shoulder and hot breakfast sausage with the Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, black pepper, garlic powder, and cumin, about 10 minutes.
Add the onion, minced garlic, pureed Hatch green chiles, potatoes, ranch seasoning, and chicken broth. Stir well.
Bring back to a simmer and cook on low about 2.5 hours.
Serve with chili-cheese pork rinds on top, if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning is Pete's own blend; use your favorite seasoning blend if you don't have it.
Pete tops his with Southern Recipe Small Batch chili-cheese pork rinds.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/JsA6e_gKzfY

title: Ranch Green Chili
time: About 1 hour at a boil, then 2.5 hours more
summary: A ranch-seasoned green chili with beef, sausage, a pound of 15-bean mix, potatoes, and a splash of beer.

ingredients.text: Garlic powder (amount not clearly specified; possibly 1 tbsp)
Black pepper (amount not clearly specified; possibly 1 tbsp)

instructions: Cook the onion with the Worcestershire, ground beef, breakfast sausage, ancho chili powder, garlic powder, black pepper, and cumin.
Add the fire-roasted tomatoes, green chiles, ranch seasoning, dried 15-bean mix, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil and cook about 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, garlic, tomato-chicken bouillon, Zippy Zap, and beer.
Cover and simmer about 2.5 hours more. Pete likes his over crackers.
notes: The transcript lists 'a tablespoon of ancho chili powder, garlic powder, black pepper, and a teaspoon of cumin.' Only the ancho and cumin amounts are clearly broken out.
Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Chuck Wagon Chili
time: About 3 hours simmering, plus searing and a 15-minute roast
summary: A from-scratch chuck wagon chili with seared cubes of chuck roast and a puree of oven-roasted garlic and peppers.

ingredients.text: 2 1/2 lb chuck roast, trimmed and cubed
A couple of tablespoons oil, for searing
Peppers, seeded (type and amount not specified)
A little oil, for roasting the garlic and peppers

instructions: Heat a couple of tablespoons of oil and sear the cubed chuck in small batches, just to brown the outside. Set the meat aside.
Add the onion and Zippy Zap to the pot and cook a few minutes, then return the meat.
Seed the peppers. Toss the peppers and 10 cloves of garlic with a little oil and roast at 350°F for 15 minutes.
Blend the roasted garlic and peppers with 1 cup beef stock until you have a chili-pepper puree, then add it to the pot.
When the meat is cooked through, add the cumin, garden-fresh tomatoes, and tomato sauce.
Cover and simmer on low 3 hours.
notes: Pete never names the peppers or says how many go into the roast, only that the seeds come out and they get pureed with the garlic.
Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; he says the link is in his bio. Use another hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Chili Cheese Dip
time: Until the vegetables soften, plus about 10 minutes to melt the cheese
summary: A party chili-cheese dip with seasoned beef, Hatch chiles, and a trio of cheeses melted with evaporated milk and cream cheese.

ingredients.text: About 1 tbsp ancho chili powder (or regular chili powder)

instructions: Brown the ground beef with the chili seasoning, onion, jalapeños, Hatch green chiles, and petite diced tomatoes.
Bring to a simmer on medium heat and cook until the vegetables soften.
Stir in the ancho chili powder and Zippy Zap.
Add the pepper jack, medium cheddar, sharp white cheddar, and evaporated milk. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and stir about every 5 minutes.
After about 10 minutes, stir in the cream cheese and keep going until everything is incorporated.
notes: Zippy Zap is Pete's own hot sauce; use another hot sauce if you don't have it.
If you don't have ancho chili powder, Pete says regular chili powder is fine.

title: Chili Cheese Tots Casserole
time: 30 minutes in the oven, then 10 minutes more with cheese (oven temperature not specified)
summary: A layered chili casserole with seasoned ground meat, beans, and cornbread mix poked down into the pot, then lined with tater tots and finished with cheese.

ingredients.text: 1 can (15 oz) beans (Pete uses pinto; use whatever you like)
2 1/2 cups cornbread mix (Pete uses a unsweetened mix; use whatever you like)
Tater tots, enough to line the top (amount not specified)

instructions: Cook the ground meat with the cayenne, cumin, black pepper, and chili powder.
Add the onion, jalapeño, and garlic (the Texas Trinity), plus the fire-roasted Rotel. Cook a few minutes to soften the vegetables.
Stir in the beans, then flatten everything out in the pan.
Add the cornbread mix and poke it down into the chili with a fork so it works in throughout.
Line tater tots over the top. Bake 30 minutes (oven temperature was not stated).
Cover with cheese and return to the oven for 10 minutes.
notes: The oven temperature is not given in the video, only the 30-minute and 10-minute times.
The amount of tater tots and cheese is not specified; cover the top.

title: Grandma's Chicken Dinner
time: 30 minutes in the oven, plus time to cook the filling
summary: Pete's grandmother called this Two-Shoe Chicken Surprise: a creamy chicken-and-vegetable filling topped with mashed potatoes and baked.

ingredients.text: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 fully cooked, deboned chicken (a rotisserie works)
Mashed potatoes, enough for a topping layer (amount not specified)
Shredded cheese, for topping (amount not specified)
Splash of Zippy Zap, to taste

instructions: Melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, bell pepper, carrots, garlic powder, black pepper, Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, and Worcestershire sauce. Cook, stirring, until the vegetables start to soften.
Stir in the flour and cook a few minutes to take the raw flour taste out.
Add the cream of chicken soup, chicken stock, and heavy cream. Stir continuously until everything is well incorporated.
Stir in the deboned chicken.
Spread a layer of mashed potatoes over the top and sprinkle with a little shredded cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes. Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete says his grandmother, born August 13, 1914, made this her whole life and named it Two-Shoe Chicken Surprise because the kids had to have both shoes on before they got a bowl.

title: Poor Man's Taco Bowls
time: About 40 minutes (30 minutes simmering, plus 10 minutes off heat)
summary: A one-pot chicken, rice, and taco-seasoned skillet meal. Pete does not add any liquid beyond the canned tomatoes, sauce, corn, and beans.

ingredients.text: 2 lb chicken thighs, trimmed and cubed
Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (amount not specified)
1 can beans (Pete uses pinto; use whatever you like)
Splash of Zippy Zap, to taste

instructions: Season the chicken all over with the cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, and Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning.
Add the onion, bell pepper, jalapeño, butter, Rotel, tomato sauce, corn, and beans. Stir in the rice until everything is well incorporated. Do not add any additional liquid.
Bring to a low simmer, cover, and cook 30 minutes.
When the 30 minutes are up you shouldn't see any liquid. Leave the lid on for 10 more minutes.
Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete says his grandmother would feed eight people for $10 with this pot.

title: Pink Chicken and Pasta
time: About 1.5 hours on high, plus time to add the sauces and pasta
summary: A crockpot chicken pasta with cream of chicken, Rotel, Alfredo, and roasted-garlic pasta sauce — the mix that turns it pink.

ingredients.text: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
16 oz roasted garlic pasta sauce (or your favorite pasta sauce)
Parmesan cheese, for topping (amount not specified)

instructions: Add the chicken, garlic powder, black pepper, Zippy Zap, smoked paprika, and Worcestershire sauce to the crockpot. Mix to coat the chicken.
Add the butter, onion, red and yellow bell peppers, jalapeño, cream of chicken soup, Hatch green chiles, Rotel, and fresh garlic. Mix well.
Cook on high for 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the Alfredo sauce, roasted garlic pasta sauce, and cream cheese until incorporated.
Fold in the al dente pasta. Top with a little Parmesan if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

title: Buffalo Ranch Chicken Torpedoes
time: About 30 minutes in the freezer, plus air-frying to 165°F
summary: Pounded chicken breasts rolled around frozen buffalo-ranch cheese sticks, breaded, and air-fried.

ingredients.text: About 1/2 cup buffalo ranch dressing (your favorite)
Chicken breasts, sliced in half and pounded thin (amount not specified)
Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the chicken (amount not specified)

instructions: Mix the mozzarella, Parmesan, cream cheese, buffalo ranch dressing, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, and Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning until well combined.
Form the mixture into cheese-stick shapes and freeze about 30 minutes.
Slice the chicken breasts in half and pound them thin. Season the chicken with Flavor-Time.
Roll each piece of chicken around a frozen cheese stick and tuck the ends in so the cheese doesn't leak out.
Coat in seasoned flour, then egg wash, then seasoned breadcrumbs.
Air-fry at 350°F, turning every couple of minutes so they cook evenly, until golden brown and 165°F inside.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete doesn't say how many chicken breasts to use; use enough halved, pounded cutlets to wrap the cheese sticks you make.

title: Poor Man's Chicken & Rice
time: About 1.5 hours in the oven, plus browning time
summary: Browned chicken leg quarters baked over seasoned rice with golden mushroom soup, onion soup mix, and mushrooms.

ingredients.text: Chicken leg quarters (amount not specified; Pete bought them on sale)
Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the chicken (amount not specified)
8 oz fresh baby bella mushrooms, sliced

instructions: Season the leg quarters on both sides with garlic powder, black pepper, smoked paprika, and Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning.
Brown them in a hot skillet with a little oil about 4 minutes per side; you're not trying to cook them through. Remove the chicken. Pour off most of the oil, leaving the browned bits in the pan.
Add the onion, celery, bell pepper, jalapeño, Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tablespoon black pepper, oregano, and Flavor-Time. Cook until the vegetables start to soften.
Stir in the garlic, Better Than Bouillon, golden mushroom soup, onion soup mix, and mushrooms. Cook a couple of minutes.
Add the rice and chicken broth and stir well.
Pour the mixture into an oven-safe dish and set the leg quarters on top. Cover tightly with foil and bake at 350°F for 1 1/2 hours.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

title: Chicken and Dumplings
time: About 45 minutes to cook the chicken, plus about 20 minutes for the dumplings
summary: A stovetop pot of chicken and dumplings with homemade buttermilk drop dumplings and a pint of heavy cream, made in an 8-quart pot.

ingredients.text: Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the chicken (amount not specified)
2 cans (10.5 oz each) cream of chicken soup
3 cups all-purpose flour, for the dumplings
About 1 tsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the dumplings
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, for the dumplings

instructions: In an 8-quart pot, melt the 1/2 stick of butter. Season the chicken breasts and skin-off leg quarters all over with Flavor-Time and brown about 4 minutes per side.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, poultry seasoning, black pepper, garlic powder, parsley, smoked paprika, and chicken stock. Stir, cover, and simmer 45 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken, debone it, and shred the breasts.
Whisk the cream of chicken soup into the pot and let it simmer a few more minutes.
For the dumplings, mix the flour, baking powder, about 1 teaspoon Flavor-Time, melted butter, and about 1 1/2 cups buttermilk to a thick drop-dumpling consistency.
Stir the heavy cream into the pot. Drop the dumpling dough in by the spoonful (Pete uses two spoons to push it off). Cook at a medium boil about 10 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken back in; don't stir hard — just push the chicken down into the pot. Simmer 7 or 8 more minutes.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
This is the from-scratch drop-dumpling version. Pete also posted a crockpot version and a buttermilk-biscuit version; those are kept as separate recipes.

title: The Best Chicken Soup
time: About 40 minutes of simmering, plus time to soften the vegetables
summary: A cheesy taco-seasoned chicken soup with ranch mix, Hatch chiles, corn, black beans, and a whole deboned chicken.

ingredients.text: 16 oz American cheese (from the grocery store deli)

instructions: In a soup pot over medium-low heat, cook the olive oil, onion, bell pepper, celery, carrots, jalapeños, and garlic until the vegetables soften.

Add the garlic powder, salt, tomato-chicken bouillon, taco seasoning, ranch seasoning, Zippy Zap, Hatch green chiles, corn, fire-roasted tomatoes, black beans, chicken broth, American cheese, and cream cheese.
Simmer on medium-low about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is incorporated.
Add the deboned chicken and simmer 10 more minutes.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

title: Crockpot King Ranch Chicken Dip
time: 30 minutes on high, then on low, stirring every 30 minutes
summary: A crockpot King Ranch-style dip with a whole deboned chicken, baby bella mushrooms, two kinds of cheese, and ranch mix.

ingredients.text: 8 oz fresh baby bella mushrooms, diced
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup with herbs
1 fully cooked, deboned chicken (boil it, bake it, buy it, or pick the crust off a bucket of chicken)
16 oz American cheese (from the grocery store deli)

instructions: Add the onion, mushrooms, jalapeños, Hatch green chiles, cream of chicken soup, Rotel, chicken, pepper jack, American cheese, chicken broth, heavy cream, ranch mix, and Zippy Zap to the crockpot.
Cook on high, covered, for 30 minutes. Stir well, then reduce to low and stir every 30 minutes until everything is soft and incorporated.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Leave the onion out if you don't like it. Pete posted another King Ranch dip with less cheese, cream, and mushrooms; that version is kept as a separate recipe.

title: The Best Chicken & Rice
time: About 5 minutes covered after it comes to a simmer, plus time to cook the chicken
summary: A stovetop chicken-and-instant-rice skillet with fire-roasted tomatoes, black beans, taco seasoning, and a sour cream finish.

ingredients.text: Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (amount not specified)
1 serrano, chopped (or a bell pepper if you prefer)
1 can (10 oz) cream of chicken soup
Shredded cheese, for topping (amount not specified)

instructions: Season the chicken thighs with cumin, Flavor-Time, and chili powder. Cook in a hot skillet with a little oil until done, then remove and shred or chop.
In the same pan, cook the onion, jalapeño, and serrano a few minutes, scraping up the browned bits. (A bell pepper can stand in for the peppers.)
Add the fire-roasted tomatoes, Hatch green chiles, cream of chicken soup, corn, black beans, and taco seasoning. Return the chopped chicken to the pan.
Stir in the instant rice, tomato-chicken bouillon, chicken stock, 1 1/2 cups shredded cheese, and sour cream until everything is incorporated.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 5 minutes. Top with more cheese and remove from the heat.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete notes you can buy the taco-seasoning packet or add the same spices one by one. He doesn't list those individual amounts.
The can of fire-roasted tomatoes is not given a size in the short.

title: Stuffed Boneless Chicken Wings
time: About 25 minutes in the air fryer, plus time to bone and stuff the wings
summary: Chicken wings with the bones pulled out, stuffed with a cream-cheese, cheddar, jalapeño, and bacon filling, then wrapped in bacon.

ingredients.text: Freshly grated cheddar cheese (amount not specified)
Creole seasoning or Zippy Zap, for the outside of the wings (amount not specified)

instructions: Cut the tip off each wing. Cut through the joint between the drumette and the flat, cut around to loosen the cartilage, then press down and pull the bones out so you have a boneless pocket.
Mix the cream cheese, cheddar, jalapeños, cooked diced bacon, Creole seasoning, granulated garlic, and Zippy Zap until well combined.
Stuff each boneless wing with the filling and season the outside a little more if you like. Wrap each wing in bacon, going end to end first and then around with another strip.
Pete says you can smoke, grill, bake, or fry them. He cooks them in the air fryer about 25 minutes.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

Pete doesn't say how many wings or how much cheddar to use. The bacon count for the filling sounded like 'six and a half slices' in the transcript; use your judgment, and have extra strips for wrapping.

title: The Best Chicken Sandwich
summary: A breakfast-style sandwich with a fried-egg cutlet, pepper jack, dill pickles, and a chicken fritter on toasted bread.

ingredients.text: Butter, for toasting the bread (amount not specified)
Bread, for the sandwiches (amount not specified)
Pepperbellypete's Zippy Zap or candy pepper sauce, to taste

instructions: Fry the eggs in a little oil about 30 seconds, spooning oil over the tops, then lift them out into seasoned flour. Coat well, dip in egg wash, and return to the seasoned flour for a second coating.
Fry until golden brown and drain.
Butter and toast the bread. When the pepper jack starts to melt, add crinkle-cut dill pickles and a chicken fritter, then close the sandwich and press it.
Finish with Zippy Zap or Pete's candy pepper sauce if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
The short never says how many eggs, fritters, or slices of bread to use, and it doesn't include a recipe for the chicken fritters themselves — Pete just adds one of his fritters to the sandwich.
Candy pepper sauce is another of Pete's sauces; use your favorite hot sauce if you don't have it.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
time: About 1.5 hours of simmering, plus time to fry the chicken and make the roux
summary: A fried-chicken-and-smoked-sausage gumbo with a dark roux, okra, and the trinity, served over rice.

ingredients.text: About 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cubed
Seasoned flour, for dusting the chicken (amount not specified)
All-purpose flour, for the roux (amount not specified)
About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the roux
1 lb okra, seared in a pan
About 2 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
Splash of Zippy Zap, to taste

instructions: Dust the cubed chicken thighs in seasoned flour and fry in oil just long enough to get a crust. Remove the chicken.
In the same oil, add all-purpose flour and about 1 tablespoon Flavor-Time. Stir continuously over medium heat until the roux is a deep color.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, smoked sausage, and seared okra. Return the chicken to the pot. Add the black pepper, garlic powder, parsley, and about 2 more tablespoons Flavor-Time.
Pour in the chicken broth, cover, and simmer about 1 1/2 hours.
Serve over rice, with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

Pete doesn't give an amount for the frying oil or the roux flour. A closely related fried chicken stew uses 1 1/2 cups oil and 1 cup seasoned flour and simmers 2 hours; that stew is kept as a separate recipe.

title: Crockpot Chicken Stroganoff
time: 6 to 8 hours on low, plus 30 minutes on high with the noodles
summary: Chicken breasts slow-cooked with three cream soups, ranch and onion soup mixes, then finished with egg noodles.

ingredients.text: About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup with herbs
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of celery soup
16 oz chicken broth, added with the noodles

instructions: Season the chicken breasts all over with about 1 tablespoon each of black pepper, garlic powder, and Flavor-Time. Add them to the crockpot with the cream of chicken, cream of celery, and golden mushroom soups, onion soup mix, ranch mix, butter, garlic, Better Than Bouillon, Zippy Zap, and 32 ounces of chicken broth. Mix well.
Cook on low 6 to 8 hours. Shred the chicken with a fork.
Turn the crockpot to high, add the egg noodles and the remaining 16 ounces of chicken broth, and cook 30 minutes.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete never says how many chicken breasts to use.

title: King Ranch Chicken
time: 35 minutes in the oven, plus time to make the filling
summary: A layered King Ranch casserole with tostadas, Rotel, cream of chicken, American cheese, and a deboned chicken, finished with Monterey Jack.

ingredients.text: Tortilla chips, crushed, for topping (amount not specified)
Monterey Jack cheese, for topping (amount not specified)
Sour cream, for serving (amount not specified)
Pico de gallo, for serving (amount not specified)

instructions: Melt the butter and soften the onion and jalapeños with the garlic powder, black pepper, and a pinch of cumin.
Add the Rotel, cream of chicken soup, American cheese, and condensed milk. Stir over medium-low heat until the cheese melts, then stir in the deboned chicken.
In an oven-safe dish, layer tostadas and the chicken mixture, repeating the layers. Top with crushed chips and Monterey Jack.
Bake 35 minutes (oven temperature not specified in the short). Serve with sour cream and pico if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

Pete says '12 ounces of condensed milk'; a 12-ounce can is the usual size for evaporated milk, so he may have meant evaporated. The short doesn't give can sizes for the Rotel or cream of chicken, or an oven temperature.
His Chicken Taco Casserole is a close variation (Velveeta, milk, taco shells, and a 350°F bake) and is kept as a separate recipe.

title: The Most Flavorful Chicken Dish
time: 8 hours on low
summary: A crockpot taco-and-ranch chicken with potatoes, carrots, Rotel, and a layer of frozen corn on top.

ingredients.text: Frozen corn, enough to line the top (amount not specified)

instructions: Toss the chicken with the taco seasoning, ranch seasoning, Mexican oregano, and cumin.
Add the onion, jalapeño, serrano, carrots, tomato-chicken bouillon, Rotel, chicken broth, lime juice, Zippy Zap, cilantro, and potatoes. Line the top with frozen corn.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

The Rotel cans are not given a size, and Pete doesn't measure the frozen corn. Texican Ranch Chicken is a closely related crockpot pot with different amounts (including 12 mini ears of corn) and is kept as a separate recipe.

title: The Best Fried Chicken
time: 8 hours to marinate, plus 30 minutes of rest and frying to 165°F
summary: A whole cut-up chicken soaked in a seasoned buttermilk-and-egg marinade, dredged in seasoned flour, and fried at 350°F.

ingredients.text: Vegetable shortening, for frying (amount not specified)

instructions: Mix the Nature's Seasons, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, black pepper, cayenne, Creole seasoning, lemon pepper, Zippy Zap, eggs, and buttermilk. Add the cut-up chicken and marinate 8 hours.
Dredge the chicken in seasoned flour and rest it on a rack 30 minutes.
Heat vegetable shortening to 350°F and fry the chicken, turning so it doesn't burn, until the internal temperature is 165°F. Finish with a little more Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
In the short Pete says 'nature seasoning'; that matches Morton Nature's Seasons, which he also calls Morton seasoning in another fried-chicken video.
Southern Fried Chicken is a close variation (garlic salt instead of garlic powder, 2 tablespoons Creole seasoning, and 3 cups buttermilk) and is kept as a separate recipe.

title: Chicken & Pasta
summary: A stovetop pot of deboned chicken and pasta in a Rotel, cream-soup, and melting-cheese sauce.

ingredients.text: Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (amount not specified)
1 lb pasta, cooked and drained (your favorite)
Splash of Zippy Zap, to taste

instructions: Melt the butter and add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic powder, black pepper, and Flavor-Time. Add the garlic and Rotel and simmer until the vegetables soften.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring back to a simmer. Stir in the cream of chicken soup, cream of mushroom soup, and melting cheese.
Add the deboned chicken and the cooked, drained pasta. Stir until everything is incorporated. Finish with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete says '16 ounces of a cheese that will melt' and doesn't give can sizes for the Rotel or cream soups.

title: Crockpot Chicken and Sausage Pasta
time: 8 to 10 hours on low, plus 30 to 40 minutes on high with the pasta
summary: Chopped chicken and smoked sausage cooked all day in the crockpot, then finished with pasta and Velveeta.

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 lb smoked sausage (Pete shows jalapeño cheese sausage)
1 bell pepper, chopped (or 3 jalapeños, whichever you prefer)
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of mushroom soup

instructions: Add the chicken, sausage, onion, celery, bell pepper or jalapeños, green onions, Rotel, cream of chicken soup, black pepper, garlic powder, tomato-chicken bouillon, Flavor-Time, cream of mushroom soup, parsley, and chicken broth to the crockpot. Stir well.
Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours.
Turn the heat to high. Stir in the pasta and Velveeta, cover, and cook 30 to 40 minutes, until the pasta is done. (Pete notes that crockpots and pastas differ.)
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete holds up jalapeño cheese sausage with the smoked sausage; the short may be jalapeño-cheese smoked sausage rather than a separate block of cheese.

title: Chicken Taco Casserole
time: 35 minutes at 350°F, plus time to make the filling
summary: A layered casserole of flat taco shells and a Rotel, cream of chicken, and Velveeta chicken filling, baked under Colby Jack.

ingredients.text: Flat taco shells, for layering (amount not specified)
About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
Fully cooked chicken (amount not specified; Pete also says it's always better with a deboned chicken)
Colby Jack cheese, for topping (amount not specified)
Sour cream, for serving (amount not specified)
Pico de gallo, for serving (amount not specified)

instructions: Grease an oven-safe dish and put down a layer of flat taco shells.

Melt the butter and cook the onion and jalapeños with the garlic powder, black pepper, cumin, Flavor-Time, and ancho chili powder. Stir in the Rotel, cream of chicken soup, Velveeta, and milk over medium-low heat until the cheese melts. Add the cooked chicken and mix well.
Layer the mixture with more taco shells, repeating as needed. On the top layer, add crumbled shells and Colby Jack.
Bake at 350°F for 35 minutes. Serve with sour cream and pico if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
The Rotel cans are not given a size, and Pete doesn't measure the taco shells, Colby Jack, or the cooked chicken in this short.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/RFx0cvPlMIo

title: Chicken & Dressing
time: 15 minutes of simmering, plus unstated baking time
summary: A Thanksgiving-style cornbread dressing with a deboned hen, boiled eggs, cream of chicken, and evaporated milk.

ingredients.text: 2 bunches green onions (1 cooked with the vegetables, 1 diced into the pan)
About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
4 cups chicken broth (3 cups simmered with the vegetables, 1 cup more in the pan)
24 oz cooked and crumbled cornbread (four 6 oz packages)
Poultry seasoning, for sprinkling over the cornbread (amount not specified)

instructions: Melt the butter and cook the onion, celery, and 1 bunch of green onions with the black pepper, poultry seasoning, garlic powder, and Flavor-Time until the vegetables soften.
Stir in the cream of chicken soup, evaporated milk, and 3 cups of the chicken broth. Bring to a low simmer and cook 15 minutes.
In a large foil pan, add the crumbled cornbread and lightly sprinkle with a little more poultry seasoning. Add 1 bunch diced green onions, the chopped boiled eggs, and the deboned hen.
Pour the hot mixture over the top, add the remaining 1 cup of broth, and mix until everything is well incorporated.
The short ends after the mixing step and does not give a baking time or temperature.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete calls for a fully cooked, deboned hen; a chicken or rotisserie chicken is the usual stand-in.

title: Fried Chicken Stew
time: 2 hours of simmering, plus time to fry the chicken and make the roux
summary: Cubed chicken thighs fried with a crust, then simmered with smoked sausage, okra, and a seasoned-flour roux. Serve over rice.

ingredients.text: Seasoned flour, for coating the chicken (amount not specified)
1 cup seasoned flour (seasoned with black pepper and Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning)
1 lb okra, seared in a skillet
Splash of Zippy Zap, to taste

instructions: Heat the oil in a pot. Lightly coat the cubed chicken thighs in seasoned flour and fry just long enough to get a crust; don't cook them all the way through. Remove the chicken once all 2 pounds are browned.
Add 1 cup seasoned flour (black pepper and Flavor-Time) to the pot. Stir continuously over medium heat until the roux is a deep color.
Add the onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, smoked sausage, and seared okra. Return the chicken to the pot. Add the garlic powder, black pepper, parsley, and another tablespoon of Flavor-Time.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cover for 2 hours.
Serve over rice, with a splash of Zippy Zap if you like.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Chicken and Sausage Gumbo is a close variation (4 ribs of celery, 1 1/2 lb sausage, and a 1 1/2-hour simmer) and is kept as a separate recipe.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/gaunsJyNfLY

title: Chicken Bombs
time: Cook to 165°F inside
summary: Thin-sliced chicken breasts rolled around a breakfast-sausage and three-cheese jalapeño filling, wrapped in bacon, and cooked to 165°F.

ingredients.text: Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning (amount not specified)
Chicken breasts, sliced thin (amount not specified)
Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning, for the chicken (amount not specified)
Barbecue sauce, for brushing (amount not specified)

instructions: Break up the breakfast sausage and cook it fully. Season with garlic powder, black pepper, parsley, and Flavor-Time. Stir in the green onions and Worcestershire sauce, then turn off the heat.
When the mixture has cooled some, mix in the cream cheese, Parmesan, Colby Jack, and pickled jalapeños.
Slice the chicken breasts thin. Put filling in the middle of each piece, season with Flavor-Time, and roll the chicken around the filling.
Wrap each roll with a strip of bacon end to end, then a couple more pieces around it.
Cook in the oven, on the grill, or in the smoker until the internal temperature is 165°F. Brush with your favorite barbecue sauce.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete doesn't say how many chicken breasts or how much bacon to use.

title: Crockpot Chicken and Dumplings
time: About 5 hours on low, plus 1.5 hours on high with the dumplings
summary: Cubed chicken and vegetables cooked in the crockpot, then finished with cheddar-buttermilk drop dumplings.

ingredients.text: About 1 tbsp Pepperbellypete's Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning
1 can (22 oz) cream of chicken soup
1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese, for the dumplings
Buttermilk, for the dumplings (amount not specified)

instructions: Add the chicken, poultry seasoning, black pepper, Flavor-Time, onion, carrots, celery, green onions, cream of chicken soup, and chicken broth to the crockpot. (Pete also uses a little water to rinse the rest of the soup out of the can.) Cover and cook on low.
After 5 hours, make the dumplings: mix the shredded cheddar, buttermilk, and 1 cup milk. Drop the dumplings into the pot.
Turn the crockpot to high, cover, and cook 1 1/2 hours.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

The short never gives a flour amount for the dumplings — Pete jumps from cheddar and buttermilk to a cup of milk and starts dropping them in. Don't invent a flour measure; use a dumpling dough you already know, or watch the video and judge the consistency.
This is the crockpot version. The stovetop drop-dumpling pot and the buttermilk-biscuit version are kept as separate recipes.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
time: 8 hours to marinate, plus 30 minutes of rest and frying to 165°F
summary: Eight pieces of chicken marinated in seasoned buttermilk and eggs, dredged in seasoned flour, and fried in shortening at 350°F.

ingredients.text: Vegetable shortening, for frying (amount not specified)

instructions: Mix the Morton seasoning, onion powder, garlic salt, smoked paprika, black pepper, cayenne, Creole seasoning, lemon pepper, Zippy Zap, eggs, and buttermilk. Add the chicken and refrigerate 8 hours.
Dredge the marinated chicken in seasoned flour and rest it on a rack 30 minutes. Let it come closer to room temperature before frying.
Heat vegetable shortening to 350°F and fry the chicken, turning so it doesn't burn, until the internal temperature is 165°F.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

One short calls the blend 'Morton seasoning'; the amounts and the rest of the marinade match the other. The 3 tablespoons of Zippy Zap and the 8 pieces of chicken are taken from the more complete telling.
The Best Fried Chicken is a close variation (garlic powder instead of garlic salt, 1 tablespoon Creole seasoning, and 4 cups buttermilk) and is kept as a separate recipe.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/7nHWvvp3Ues

title: Broccoli-Chicken Casserole
time: About 10 minutes on the stove and 1 hour in the oven (45 minutes covered, 15 uncovered)
summary: A baked casserole of cooked chicken, broccoli, and cauliflower in a cream-of-chicken and cheese sauce, topped with mozzarella and cheddar.

ingredients.text: 1 can (10 oz) cream of chicken soup
16 oz American cheese (from the grocery store deli)
4 cups fully cooked chicken (boil it, bake it, or buy a rotisserie)

instructions: Melt the butter and cook the onion with the Zippy Zap, garlic powder, black pepper, smoked paprika, and cayenne. Add the cauliflower, cream of chicken soup, American cheese, half-and-half, cream cheese, chicken, and broccoli.
Cook on low about 10 minutes, until the cauliflower starts to soften, and mix well.
Spread into a greased oven-safe dish and top with the mozzarella and cheddar. Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes, then uncover and bake 15 minutes more (about 1 hour total).
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

In one telling the half-and-half sounds like 'a cup and a half, a half and a half' — 1 1/2 cups half-and-half. The 2 tablespoons of Zippy Zap and the total one-hour bake come from the other posting of this same casserole.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/IlhNBgIhadc

title: Crockpot Chicken Rigatoni
time: 2 hours on low, plus 45 minutes after adding the pasta
summary: Four chicken breasts slow-cooked with cream of chicken, cream cheese, and heavy cream, then finished with rigatoni, Parmesan, and smoked Gouda.

ingredients.text: 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 1/2 cups chicken broth, added with the pasta

instructions: Add the chicken breasts, Italian seasoning, black pepper, garlic powder, onion soup mix, cream of chicken soup, heavy cream, butter, cream cheese, 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, and Zippy Zap to the crockpot. Stir, cover, and cook on low for 2 hours.
Shred the chicken with forks.
Stir in the rigatoni, Parmesan, the remaining 1 1/2 cups chicken broth, and the smoked Gouda. Cover and cook 45 minutes more.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/E6SI4IhNO9w

title: Chicken Pot Pie
time: 35 minutes in the oven, plus time to cook the filling
summary: A double-crust pot pie filled with a whole deboned chicken, bacon, fried potatoes, and a cream-of-chicken gravy.

ingredients.text: Black pepper, for the potatoes (amount not specified)
Garlic, for the potatoes (amount not specified)
1 can (10 oz) cream of chicken soup
Pie crust, for a bottom and top crust (amount not specified)

instructions: Cook the chopped bacon until done; remove it from the pot. In the same pot, cook the diced potatoes with salt, pepper, and garlic until they're cooked through, then remove them.

Add the onion, celery, carrots, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, black pepper, oregano, garlic powder, and poultry seasoning. Stir in the heavy cream, butter, thyme, chicken stock, and cream of chicken soup. Bring back to a simmer and reduce a little.
Stir in the deboned chicken, cooked potatoes, and bacon.
Fit a pie crust into a greased oven-safe dish, add the filling, and cover with the top crust. Bake 35 minutes (oven temperature not specified in the short).
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete doesn't give an oven temperature or a brand or size for the pie crusts.

title: Tuscan Chicken and Pasta
time: About 30 minutes after the chicken is cooked (20 minutes for the pasta, plus 10 more)
summary: Thin-sliced chicken breasts with a one-pot cherry-tomato, spinach, Parmesan, and pasta sauce.

ingredients.text: Oregano, for the chicken (amount not specified)
Black pepper, for the chicken (amount not specified)
Crushed red pepper flakes (amount not specified)

instructions: Season about 6 thin-sliced chicken breasts with smoked paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper. Cook in a hot skillet with a little oil until cooked through, then remove from the pan.

Add the onion and Worcestershire sauce and sweat them down. Stir in the cherry tomatoes, garlic, garlic powder, black pepper, oregano, crushed red pepper flakes, tomato paste, heavy cream, chicken stock, spinach, Parmesan, and pasta.
Cook on low 20 minutes. Set the chicken back on top and cook 10 minutes more. Stir it all together or just scoop it out.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
The 6 cutlets, 1 cup of chicken stock, and extra 10 minutes come from the more complete telling of this same pot. The other short doesn't measure the stock.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lv3L0nTB_ZU

title: Chicken and Dumplings with Buttermilk Biscuits
time: About 15 minutes covered after the biscuits go in, plus time to soften the vegetables
summary: A stovetop pot of chicken and dumplings that uses canned buttermilk biscuits instead of from-scratch dough.

ingredients.text: 1 can (22 oz) cream of chicken soup
1 fully cooked, deboned chicken (Pete uses a large chicken)
3 cans (7.5 oz each) small buttermilk biscuits

instructions: Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the onion, carrots, celery, and Worcestershire sauce until the vegetables start to soften.
Add the black pepper, Nature's Seasoning, and parsley. Whisk in the cream of chicken soup, chicken broth, and milk and bring back to a boil.
Stir in the deboned chicken. Cut the biscuits in half and drop them into the pot.
Bring back to a slow boil over medium heat, cover, and cook 15 minutes.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Pete says 'nature's seasoning' here; that matches Morton Nature's Seasons in his other videos.
This is the biscuit-dumpling version. The from-scratch drop dumplings and the crockpot pot are kept as separate recipes.

title: Texican Ranch Chicken
time: 8 hours on low
summary: A crockpot taco-and-ranch chicken with potatoes, carrots, Rotel, and a top layer of mini ears of corn.
instructions: Toss the chicken with the taco seasoning, ranch seasoning, Mexican oregano, and cumin until well coated.
Add the onion, jalapeños, serranos, carrots, tomato-chicken bouillon, Rotel, chicken broth, lime juice, Zippy Zap, cilantro, and potatoes. Lay the 12 mini ears of corn on top.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

The Most Flavorful Chicken Dish is a closely related crockpot pot with different amounts (2 1/2 lb chicken, fewer peppers and carrots, and an unmeasured layer of frozen corn) and is kept as a separate recipe.

title: Birria Chicken Dip
time: 4 hours on low, plus time to blend and melt the cheese
summary: Chicken breasts slow-cooked with dried chiles and tomatoes, blended into a consommé, then finished as a queso dip.

ingredients.text: 4 ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
8 guajillo chiles, stems and seeds removed
5 árbol chiles, stems and seeds removed

instructions: Add the onion, tomatoes, ancho, guajillo, and árbol chiles, chicken breasts, garlic, Mexican oregano, peppercorns, salt, cumin, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, and chicken stock to the crockpot. Push everything down, stir, cover, and cook on low for 4 hours.
Remove the chicken. Lift out the vegetables, blend them, and return the puree and the chicken to the crockpot.
Stir in the queso quesadilla, pepper jack, Zippy Zap, and evaporated milk until the dip comes together.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.

title: One-Pot Chicken and Orzo
time: About 20 minutes of simmering, plus time to finish the orzo
summary: A skillet of deboned chicken, orzo, broccoli, and American cheese finished with a little heavy cream.

ingredients.text: Crushed red pepper flakes (amount not specified)
4 cups fully cooked chicken (a whole deboned chicken)

instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter. Add the onion, Zippy Zap, garlic, black pepper, crushed red pepper flakes, and garlic powder.
Stir in the broccoli, orzo, chicken stock, cooked chicken, and American cheese. Bring to a simmer on low and cook about 20 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and keep cooking, stirring, until the pasta is done.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
Also shown in: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/bCgIa55523g

title: King Ranch Chicken Dip
time: About 1 hour in the crockpot (30 minutes, then 30 more after stirring)
summary: A quicker King Ranch dip with 4 cups of cooked chicken, pepper jack, American cheese, mushrooms, and ranch mix.

ingredients.text: 1 can cream of chicken soup with herbs

title: Creamy Chicken Noodle Soup

instructions: Melt the butter and cook the onion, carrots, and celery with the Zippy Zap, black pepper, smoked paprika, poultry seasoning, Cajun Two-Step, and tomato-chicken bouillon until the vegetables start to soften. Add the garlic.
Stir in the white American cheese, heavy cream, deboned chicken, and 8 cups of chicken stock. Bring back to a simmer, cover, and cook about 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and the remaining 2 cups of chicken broth. Simmer about 20 minutes, until the pasta is done.

title: Chicken à la Delicious
time: 30 minutes in the freezer, then cook to 165°F
summary: Chicken breasts chilled in the freezer, dipped in Zippy Zap buttermilk, and double-coated in seasoned flour and breadcrumbs.
instructions: Put the chicken breasts in the freezer about 30 minutes so they firm up.
Whisk the buttermilk with the Zippy Zap. Dip the chicken in the buttermilk, then into seasoned flour, back into the buttermilk, and then into seasoned breadcrumbs.
Cook until the internal temperature is 165°F. The short doesn't spell out whether Pete fries, bakes, or air-fries them.
notes: Flavor-Time Southern Seasoning and Zippy Zap are Pete's own products; swap in your favorite seasoning blend or hot sauce if you don't have them.
